answer_raw.explanation: The titer loss began after the feed-water line fitting was replaced. The new fitting leaches a chelatable metal ion into the culture. This metal causes broth turbidity (aggregation/precipitation) and suppresses secreted product titer — the broth 'looked cloudier than usual at harvest,' matching this. Evidence: (1) Turning the feed off restored titer to 65 vs ~35 at feed=25, implicating the feed-water source. (2) Holding feed=100 constant and varying ONLY the chelator produced a clean dose-response — titer rose 17.9->56.8->57.9 as chelator went 30->60->90, while turbidity fell 46.7->11.2->6.06. Because feed was held fixed, turbidity's inverse relationship with titer is causal, not a feed confound. (3) DO was constant (~55) across conditions, so DO drift and the temperature-excursion theories are ruled out; DO and VCD are bystanders/decoys. Decisive test: fixed feed, varied chelator — titer followed turbidity down then up, establishing the metal->turbidity->titer-loss chain. Recommend dosing the metal-chelating additive at ~75 (past the 60 knee, on the plateau, safe margin below the untested overdose region). Reducing feed-water flow also helps (removes the metal source) but the chelator is the practical fix that keeps feeding intact.
